objective: Fix the VS Code extension route-publication seam so activation, reload, restored tabs and live mux observation publish the exact current Codex thread for the exact repo/window, eliminating manager/shared-registry split-brain without fabricating routes.

production_seam.notes: Real production publication path (activation getMcpClient, lease-renewal timer renewWindowRouteLease, and selectCoordinatorTarget all converge through this one function) -- no test-only helper was added disconnected from production.

acceptance_checks.description: A route becomes available only when exactly one fresh, ready, extension-owned mux instance matches repo_id, parent_pid (extension host), and has a bare UUID active_thread_id.
Verified thread_id/session_id is written into both the repo-local coordinator-targets.json and the shared router manifest for the same repo/window lease.
Empty, synthetic codex:window, wrong repo, wrong extension host, wrong window, stale, not-ready, and ambiguous owners all remain route_pending.
A previously-verified foreign or current-window route in the shared manifest is never overwritten by a pending/ambiguous observation, unless its lease has expired.

Reload/activation/restored-tab/runtime-repair and later live mux observation all converge through the same refreshCoordinatorRouteOwnership call with no polling loop, recursive startup, CLI fallback, or process killing.
Thread ids are never derived from window_id/repo_id/claim_episode; only a literal active_thread_id read from a matching live mux registry file is ever published.
